newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam to meet GDP goal, worried by low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam to meet GDP goal, worried by low inflation.

text.p: HANOI, Sept 11 (Reute) - Vietnam is in a good position to achieve its target of 9-10 percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year, the deputy prime minister in charge of economic affairs said on Friday.

Tran Duc Luong told a meeting of the International Cultural Exchange Club that the government was also confident industrial output would pick up in the last four months of the year, making achievement of a 14-14.5 percent output growth target possible.
But he indicated concern about the recent drop in consumer prices and said measures may have to be taken in the remaining months of the year to prevent deflation.

On inflation, which has declined every month since May and now stands at an annual rate of 3.2 percent compared with 18.4 percent a year earlier, Luong said the authorities may have given the economy an "overdose" of anti-inflation measures.
"We consider that if the inflation drops too drastically then, it could affect the economy in terms of business operations and production," he said.
"So, in the the remaining months of the year, possibly we have to take some measures in order to keep the inflation rate going going down to below zero," he added.
He gave no details of what measures would be taken.
The central State Bank of Vietnam has recently been engineering lower interest rates to stimulate lending, and there are plans to ease credit limits on commercial banks.
